about: Overly Attached Girlfriend is a webcam close-up of vlogger Laina Morris staring into the lens with wide, unblinking eyes and a tight, too-sweet smile, her head tilted slightly forward. The expression reads as affection about to turn into surveillance. Captions cast her as the clingiest partner imaginable: someone who checks your inbox, memorizes your schedule and turns every innocent comment into proof of devotion or betrayal, all delivered in a cheerful tone that makes it creepier.
origin: Laina Morris uploaded a parody of Justin Bieber's song "Boyfriend" to YouTube in June 2012, singing intensely possessive lyrics. A still of her stare from the video became one of the defining advice-animal image macros of 2012.
usage:
Use the classic top-and-bottom layout. The top line sounds sweet or ordinary; the bottom line reveals the alarming, obsessive reason behind it. The twist always comes in the bottom box.

It lands best when the reveal is specific and slightly too organized: tracking, scheduling, screenshots, spreadsheets. It also works for apps, brands and services that act clingy, like a streaming service asking if you're still watching or a shopping app that knows where you were.
